summary.name: GitUp
summary.one_liner: GitUp is a free, open-source macOS Git client that visualizes branches and merges in a live graph and offers undo and snapshot history for repo changes.
use_cases: visualize branches and merges in a repository
undo or back out of unwanted local changes
rewrite, split, reorder, or squash commits
search commits, branches and tags by message, author or diff
learn Git safely as a beginner
build custom Git apps with GitUpKit
summary.what_it_does: GitUp is a Git client with a live graph that updates immediately when repo changes are made, including changes made outside GitUp. It supports undo/redo via cmd-z and a Snapshot feature that records every change to the repo so you can step back to any earlier point. Commit operations include rewrite, split, delete, reorder, fixup, squash, cherry-pick, merge and rebase. The page also says GitUp reads the repo database directly rather than calling the Git binary, and includes search across branches, tags and commits, plus quick view of commit messages and diffs via the spacebar. GitUp ships with GitUpKit, a toolkit for building Git apps.
notable: Live map graph updates instantly for changes made inside or outside GitUp
Snapshot feature gives Time-Machine-like history of repo changes
Bundles GitUpKit toolkit for building custom Git apps
Reads the repo database directly instead of calling the Git binary, per the page
caveats: Support is through GitHub Issues and docs; no formal support stated
